title: Project Proposal Specs
text:
Each player unit fires a coded IR packet when the trigger is pressed.
FPGA generates a 38 kHz ± 2% IR carrier, verified with an oscilloscope capture.
A player unit registers a hit on its single hit zone when struck by the other player’s blaster from at least 5 m indoors.
IR receiver input is passed through a synchronizer before being decoded on the FPGA.
IR decoder rejects packets with invalid timing or check bits.
Hits are not registered from a player’s own shots or from stray IR sources (e.g., a TV remote).
IR decoder testbench passes, verifying valid and invalid packets.





Each player unit has three hit zones, and the FPGA decodes all three IR receivers in parallel.
Hits register from at least 10 m indoors.
Decoder testbench covers the edges of the timing acceptance window and simultaneous packets on multiple receivers.

title: Project Proposal Specs
text:
Game Logic and Data

Proficiency

Game progresses through start, play, out, and game over states, with a reset returning both units to start.
A valid hit decrements the hit player’s health.
SPI interconnect between the MCU and FPGA is wired correctly and transfers hit events (shooter ID, zone) and game state.
MCU handles hit events with an interrupt rather than polling.



Excellence

Hits are scored by zone.
SPI communication between the MCU and FPGA is displayed on the logic analyzer.
Finite state machines are implemented in an appropriate form discussed in lecture: canonical, non-canonical, or communicating.

title: Project Proposal Specs
text:
Display and Audio Feedback

Proficiency

Indicator LEDs show each player’s health and game state, and flash on a valid hit.
Win/lose is shown on each unit at game over.
MCU plays sampled sound effects through its DAC, with sample timing driven by a hardware timer.
A hit sound effect plays on each valid hit.



Excellence

LED display animations are stored in SPRAM and played back on command from the MCU.
Distinct sound effects play for firing, hits, and win/lose.

title: Project Proposal Specs
text:
Web Server and Scoreboard

Proficiency

MCU sends hit events to the ESP8266 over UART, and the ESP8266 delivers them to the laptop server.
Laptop server logs hit events from both player units.



Excellence

Scoreboard web page displays each player’s health, hits by zone, and win/lose, updating within 1 s of a hit.
Games can be started and reset from the scoreboard web page.

title: Project Proposal Specs
text:
Hardware and Power

Proficiency

Both units run untethered on battery power inside 3D-printed housings with straps.
Logic is broken into modules (e.g., IR transmitter, IR decoder, SPI peripheral, LED driver), with control logic separate from datapath logic.



Excellence

A full 15-minute two-player game runs on battery without resets or dropped hits.
Measured average current per unit is within 20% of the calculated power budget (≈180 mA).

title: E155 Final Project
text: We will build a two-player infrared laser tag system in which each player carries a blaster and a wearable target, both driven by one E155 development board (iCE40 UP5K FPGA + STM32L432KC MCU). Pulling the trigger fires a coded IR packet; when another player’s receivers decode it, their unit registers a hit, flashes its LEDs, plays a sound effect, and reports the hit over Wi-Fi to a laptop scoreboard.

title: Project Proposal
text:
We will build a two-player infrared laser tag system in which each player carries a blaster and a wearable target, both driven by one E155 development board (iCE40 UP5K FPGA + STM32L432KC MCU). Pulling the trigger fires a coded IR packet; when another player’s receivers decode it, their unit registers a hit, flashes its LEDs, plays a sound effect, and reports the hit over Wi-Fi to a laptop scoreboard.



Each player unit contains the following:

Blaster: a 940 nm IR LED behind a focusing lens, driven at a 38 kHz carrier, plus a push-button trigger.
Target: two IR receivers in the baseline (front and back), expandable to six (chest, back, both shoulders) so hits can be scored by body segment.
Feedback: indicator LEDs showing a hit, a speaker for hit as well as win/lose sound effects.
Connectivity: an ESP8266 that streams hit events to a laptop running a polling scoreboard web page.
Enclosure: a 3D-printed housing and straps, powered by a portable battery so players can move freely.




The project exercises the core course concepts:

LED display driving (Lab 1)
Input synchronization (Lab 3)
Timer-driven audio (Lab 4)
Interrupts (Lab 5)
IoT streaming (Lab 6)

The new hardware is the IR transmit/receive chain; the new FPGA content is SPRAM-backed display patterns; the new MCU content is DAC-based audio.
